messages:
ben: Quick RFC follow-up re: canary flip-flops. We had a case where late probe verdicts from aggregators overturned a decider change and caused traffic thrash. Need a clear contract: who owns ordering?

tara: Short answer: decider should be the sequencer. Observers can emit signals but must tag them so the decider can order/ignore stale ones.

jess: Agreed. Two low-cost options: (1) epoch token minted by decider and carried by probes, or (2) make decider idempotent by seq+dedupe window. I prefer epoch token + small seq.

otto: Epoch token sounds good. Implementation sketch: decider increments rollout_epoch and issues lease_id in decision. Aggregators stamp incoming probe batches with that lease_id when known. Observers still emit without blocking.

ben: Concrete fields: probe -> {verdict, metric, value, ts, probe_epoch?, lease_id?}. Decision -> {action, rollout_epoch, seq, apply_until, fallback_hints[]}. Keep fields optional for backcompat.

jess: For fallback_hints, runtime needs a ranked short list. Examples: [{type:variant,id:A,score:95},{type:quantized,id:q4,score:70}]. Limit to top 2-3 to keep hot path O(1).

tara: Also include reason codes (p95>300ms) and a trace_id emitted by decider so telemetry can join decision -> signals -> user impact.

otto: Bandwidth concern: high-QPS probes. Mitigations: quantize epoch (only bump on decision), sample probes, and have aggregators compress repeated identical verdicts per window. Use compact protobuf wire for probes.

ben: Backcompat: treat missing epoch/lease as low-confidence verdicts; decider can weight them lower or ignore if confidence absent. Add compatibility flag so rollout can opt into strict-mode.

jess: Test plan: e2e that injects late-stale probes after a decision and asserts decider ignores those with epoch<current. Also chaos test with aggregator delays to ensure no thrash.

tara: Long-term: consider a tiny decision-plane commit log (append-only) that records decisions with seq and TTL. Useful for ordered replay and post-incident analysis. Medium-term only.

otto: Runtime selection when multiple hints exist: runtime should pick first compatible hint from ranked list. If none compatible, apply a cheap default fallback and emit an alert. Don't ask runtime to score hints heavily. Keep scoring server-side.

ben: Observability: telemetry event for decision_commit: {seq, epoch, apply_until, shifted_percent, trace_id, hints_count}. Also emit probe_aggregator events with stamped epoch for correlation.

ci-bot: ci: canary-decider v0.1 -> canary rolling out us-east-1 7% :rocket:

jess: Action items: - ben: small PR to add probe_epoch, lease_id, confidence fields to observer proto (opt-in) - tara: perf microbench for runtime hint application and aggregator compression - otto: draft RFC for decision-plane commit log and replay semantics - all: define telemetry event schema + e2e that injects late probes

ben: Timeline: ship opt-in epoch fields this sprint (compatibility flag on by default for older SDKs). Decision-plane follow-up next quarter. Any objections?

tara: +1. Keep hint lists tiny. Add rate-limit on probe verdicts per-aggregator to avoid floods.

jess: I'll add a short postmortem template to the PR and a checklist for verifying no thrash in canary dashboards.

ben: Thanks everyone. This should make the observer/decider boundary explicit and remove accidental ordering flaps. Ping me for pairing on the PR.
